caption: Supplementary Fig. 25 | Environmental associations with alternative near-peak durations. a,b, Environmental coefficient differences between F and U duration models (GB; a) and between U and R models (GL; b). Factors are SST, 200–850-hPa shear, mid-level RH, 200-hPa divergence, 500-hPa ascent and hemisphere-signed 850-hPa vorticity. Both comparisons use 2,232 equal-weight SIDs and the same common-entry design, with rank 21 and 2,211 residual degrees of freedom. Effects are log-duration differences per fixed common-entry environmental SD. Dark circles and bars show primary marginal 95% HC3/Student-t intervals with 2,211 degrees of freedom; blue squares and bars show auxiliary 95% SID-percentile intervals from 2,000 valid draws. The separated markers share one point estimate and differ only in uncertainty method. P values use the primary analytic reference, with Benjamini–Hochberg adjustment across all twelve tests. All q values exceed 0.05 (minimum ). These are conditional duration associations, without a causal interpretation. Source tables provide P/q, both interval estimates, reference SDs and sample sizes.
